sentences.text: Amina Hussain is the health visitor.
Jade Turner is the mother.
Today is Leo's two-year review.
Amina will check on Poppy during the visit.
Amina will make notes on Leo and Poppy.
Amina will share concerns about children's safety if she is worried.
Leo is saying about twenty words: mama, car, more, bye-bye, dog.
Leo is putting two words together, such as 'more juice'.
Leo is running and climbing, including climbing the bookcase last week.
Leo is fussy about food; eats toast, pasta, yoghurt.
Poppy is fed by bottles, about six a day.
Poppy has started on baby rice.
Poppy has a nappy rash that is broken in places.
Poppy's nappy rash has lasted about a week.
Jade has been applying Sudocrem to Poppy's rash.
Jade ran out of nappies on Sunday and has been leaving them on longer.
Food in the house includes bread, some cereal, and one tin of Poppy's milk.
The milk supply for Poppy is one tin, until Friday.
The milk supply ends on Friday, when Jade's Universal Credit comes in.
Jade is worried about losing her job and being evicted.
Jade has not received any letters from the landlord or notices of eviction.
Jade has paid rent up to date and is concerned about future rent payments.
Jade started a cleaning job at the retail park in September.
Jade's cleaning job is at night, from ten to twelve, sometimes half past twelve.
Jade's friend Shannon looks after Leo and Poppy while she is at work.
Shannon cannot always look after the children.
When Shannon cannot look after the children, Jade leaves them alone for a couple of hours, while they are asleep.
The children are left alone for about a couple of hours, and the flat is locked.
Jade leaves the children alone for three nights a week, since Shannon got her new job.
Jade's mother is in Northby and would help if contacted.
